title: Opening the studio with Marshall Sehorn
summary: The studio opened out of necessity because the other local studio lagged; Sehorn handles day-to-day business.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Going into some more up-to-date things. When did you open the studio? Yeah. Maybe five years now.
We could be more accurate downstairs.
Was there any particular thing that prompted you to do it or did you just want to control your own sound and provide an outlet for local musicians?

The studio came about out of necessity. The other studio in town, and I would say at that time, the studio in town, wasn't quite keeping up to certain standards. I'm sure that even they would have liked themselves. It just wasn't quite up to date on a lot of things. Marshall and I decided that if we could pull it off to get one going. It was actually designed for us to do our own recordings here. Shortly after opening, we learned that you don't open the studio just to record yourself.
So you've had a working relationship with Marshall Seahorn for almost 15 years?
Well, I guess it could be it. It's legitimate. Ladder 65. 65.
What aspects does he handle here in the studio now? He's a go-getter.
Contracts coming in, going out. In voices, who holds, who...
A lot of the day-to-day business operations. Oh, yes.
